history.new: The longest game can be computed with O(log^2 n) moves: L(n) = Psi(lazy(n)) + (length of the strategy game of Cusenza et al. started at the lazy representation), whose second phase has at most B(n) - Psi(lazy(n)) <= 1 + (t+1)(t+6)/2 moves (t the top level of lazy(n)); correct whenever [C, Thm 1.2] is (like Theorem 4). The published method plays about phi^2 n moves. The conjectured recursion (CLM-C19-05) gives the same values at the same speed.
history.old: The recursion of CLM-C19-05 evaluates L(n) with O(log^2 n) arithmetic operations; the published method (playing the split-first game) needs L(n) ~ phi^2 n moves. On the tested range both agree.
